title: A Meteor Shower Is Happening Tonight: Can We See It In Raleigh?
excerpt: North Carolina may see streaks of light across Earth's atmosphere tonight.
content:
North Carolina may see streaks of light across Earth’s atmosphere tonight.

The Orionids meteor shower is expected to be active from Friday, Oct. 2 until Saturday, Nov. 7, with a peak the night of Wednesday, Oct. 21 and Oct. 22.

“Orionid meteors are known for their brightness and for their speed,” according to NASA. “These meteors are fast – they travel at about 41 miles per second into Earth’s atmosphere. Fast meteors can leave glowing “trains” (incandescent bits of debris in the wake of the meteor) which last for several seconds to minutes. Fast meteors can also sometimes become fireballs: Look for prolonged explosions of light when viewing the Orionid meteor shower.”

ISS Orbital Radar tracker noted that the forecast to see the meteor shower in Raleigh and surrounding Triangle areas is fair; however, the city lights may interfere heavily with the chances.

According to the News & Observer, the best places to view the meteor shower in North Carolina are:

  • Brunswick Islands, including the Ingram Planetarium in Sunset Beach
  • Great Smoky Mountains National Park
  • Starlight Hills Campground near South Mountains State Park
  • Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute
  • Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
